pillar_reactions.evidence: Full presentation delivered from 00:42:00 — daily training structured so the body can handle it, 30-40 minutes three to four times a week, bespoke mobility protocols for the knee and back, and the six-month self-sufficiency frame ("after those six months, you won't need him anymore... He will teach you how to fish"). Asked "in terms of training and mobility, does that make sense for you where you're at?" the prospect said "Yeah, it does make sense, it does make sense" and on questions "No". Notable that his only response to the invitation for questions was to disclose a new injury: "the only thing I forgot to mention is, I think I've just literally fractured my finger, so I'm still training." He was already pre-sold on the modality before the pillar was presented — "my understanding of kettlebells and my previous experience of them is that actually it's kind of both at the same time" — so this pillar had little work to do.

Presented at 00:46:08 as no calorie counting and no macros, built on three variables — what you eat, when you eat, how much you eat — plus an eight-hour eating window and whole foods. This landed well because it matched a preference the prospect had already stated: "I don't like restrictions. If you try and restrict me, I'll tell you to get lost... when someone says, look, you can eat as many vegetables as you want, that frees me in my head." Asked for questions he said "Yeah, I understand that... Not really. No, I don't. No, I don't." Accepted rather than enthusiastic — he had already independently arrived at intermittent fasting ("The earliest I would eat is 11"), so the pillar largely described what he already does, and his actual stated failure point, late-night snacking after dinner, was acknowledged but never given a mechanism.

Presented at 00:49:32 as the app, weekly check-ins with form feedback, video review of movements and Trevor's personal cell number. The prospect agreed the principle firmly — "accountability obviously is critical. It's key to success. I understand that" and "It does. Absolutely, it does" — but declined to engage further and reserved judgement: "it's one of those things I think you have to just experience it and then give feedback accordingly... you're not going to know until you actually start that interaction." This is the pillar he most needed and the one he probed least, and the rep did not connect it back to the accountability substitute the prospect had already named as superior to human trainers.

anchors.raw: I'm due to potentially have a conversation next week with another trainer because he, unlike other trainers, is a specialist in diabetes. And that's why I am still going to have that conversation with him.
anchors.note: A live competing provider positioned on exactly the axis this prospect cares about most — his diagnosed disease. No price was attached to it because no price was attached to anything on this call, so it undercuts on differentiation rather than on cost. Primal was presented with zero clinical or metabolic positioning, which leaves the specialist unopposed on the only criterion the prospect named.

anchors.raw: when I was training 10 years ago with that bodybuilder... He got me to the point where the GP said, how did you perform this miracle? ... My HbA1c came down to less than six, which is just normal, from a lot higher, from double that.
anchors.note: Strongly supportive. He has paid for one-to-one coaching before, it produced a clinically verified result, and he attributes that result to the coach rather than to himself. He also volunteered the prescription that made it work — "I said to him, Michael, what do you want me to do when I'm not with you? There's nothing. You don't need to do anything. Just train with me" — which is a direct precedent for a structured programme with an authority figure. The rep never used it as price justification because he never got to price.

anchors.raw: it gives me immediate feedback, which is amazing. It's really, really good. In fact, be perfectly honest with you, it's the thing that keeps you most accountable is that. I've never had, you know, I've had trainers before, but it doesn't keep me as accountable as having that live feedback minute by minute.
anchors.note: The prospect explicitly rated a cheap device above every human trainer he has hired on the accountability dimension — which is the pillar Primal charges most heavily for. He immediately qualified it ("Well, whenever I choose to look at it"), which is the opening to reframe device data as information versus a coach as intervention. The rep did not take it, and delivered the accountability pillar 30 minutes later without ever referencing the comparison.

anchors.raw: even if you don't think I'm a good fit, I'm going to do this anyway, whether it's with you guys or not. I think kettlebells is a really good way forward for me, even if it's not with you.
anchors.note: Stated at 00:11:14, before any presentation. The prospect has already decided to adopt the modality regardless of vendor, which removes the modality itself as a reason to pay. Everything Primal charges for therefore has to be carried by structure and accountability, not by kettlebells — and the rep spent most of the presentation on kettlebell mechanics.

unmet_demand.want: Coaching from someone with specific expertise in managing type 2 diabetes, so that training and nutrition are built around glycaemic control and HbA1c rather than around general fitness.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme was presented as generic kettlebell coaching. The only diabetes-specific content offered was an unsourced remark that "for diabetes, intermittent fasting is, has some very good, good effect" and a note that cheat meals would go on the back burner. No metabolic credential, protocol, CGM integration or clinical track record was offered, and the rep did not ask what the specialist would give him that Trevor would not.

unmet_demand.want: Loaded training that is genuinely safe around a grade 2 L5-S1 spondylolisthesis and an arthritic post-ACL right knee, with a stated method for handling the flare-ups he already gets.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asserted the programme would work around it — "the whole program also is going to be working around your knee injury. So we, we need to strengthen that" and "This is something we need to work around, but not totally excluded" — but this was a claim, not a mechanism, and it was made without any clinician being consulted. The prospect stated plainly that he does not know how to manage the flare-ups: "I don't know how to manage that, to be perfectly honest with you. I don't know what to do, because it then hurts quite a bit." That question was left unanswered.

unmet_demand.want: Help changing his relationship with food, which he identifies as a trauma-driven coping mechanism rather than a knowledge or planning problem.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He was explicit that this is the root: "I don't drink alcohol. I don't smoke anymore. I don't do drugs. I do food", and "So I need to change my relationship with food." The nutrition pillar answers what, when and how much — a structure and content solution to a stated emotional-regulation problem. Nothing in the offer addresses the behaviour under stress, and his own history shows structure alone has failed before: "when I did eventually have it, I lost it again."
